goal: Guide the developer to build the Windows-on-ARM MAUI HybridWebView app with an ARM64 configuration instead of Any CPU.
must_include: Uses the `%1 is not a valid Win32 application` message and Windows ARM context to suspect an architecture mismatch, not bad HTML content.
Identifies `<PlatformTarget>AnyCPU</PlatformTarget>` as suspect for this Windows MAUI/HybridWebView ARM64 case.
Recommends creating/selecting an ARM64 platform configuration and building/publishing with matching ARM64 platform and runtime identifier, then cleaning/rebuilding.
Notes that HybridWebView/Blazor Hybrid depends on the platform web view, so the architecture of native components matters.
must_not: Tell the developer to remove HybridWebView because it is unsupported on Windows.
Suggest copying x64 native DLLs into an ARM64 publish as a fix.
Focus only on reinstalling Visual Studio or the .NET SDK while ignoring the project platform.
acceptable_alternatives: Use separate x64 and ARM64 publish profiles instead of a single Any CPU publish.
Temporarily run an x64 build under emulation only as a diagnostic, not as the ARM64 fix.
solved: The answer changes the Windows build/publish to a matching ARM64 configuration and explains why Any CPU is the wrong clue in this scenario.
partial: The answer recognizes a native architecture mismatch but does not point to the Any CPU project setting or ARM64 configuration.
notes: The source issue was closed as a duplicate of a Blazor Hybrid issue; the reported workaround was using a real ARM64 configuration instead of Any CPU.
